1	# ADR-0005: Freeze configuration v1 and separate structural from semantic validation
2	
3	- Status: Accepted
4	- Date: 2026-07-10
5	- Owners: Repository maintainer
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	The alpha decoder already called its configuration `version: 1`, but no public schema or compatibility
10	promise defined what that version meant. Editor validation, runtime validation, and future package
11	upgrades could therefore disagree or silently reinterpret an existing repository.
12	
13	JSON Schema can describe object shape, bounds, enumerations, and many string constraints. It cannot
14	reliably express every cross-entry invariant used here, including Unicode/case-normalized path
15	collisions, adapter-to-source ownership, symbolic links, and actual filesystem budgets.
16	
17	## Decision
18	
19	Package SemVer and configuration versions are independent:
20	
21	- npm package versions describe CLI/API releases;
22	- the integer `version` in `config.yaml` describes the canonical data contract.
23	
24	Configuration v1 is the first beta contract. Every raw configuration accepted by the v1 runtime
25	decoder must also pass `schemas/config-v1.schema.json`. The reverse is intentionally not guaranteed:
26	runtime validation adds documented semantic and filesystem rules that JSON Schema cannot express.
27	Strings are not silently trimmed; surrounding whitespace is invalid.
28	
29	The v1 schema has a stable `$id`, is shipped in the npm package, and is copied into each initialized
30	repository. `sync` repairs a missing or drifted copied schema but does not rewrite canonical YAML.
31	A pre-schema v1 project remains runnable; `validate` warns when the editor directive is missing and
32	documents the exact manual addition.
33	
34	Unknown configuration versions fail before mutation. There is no migration command while v1 is the
35	only version. A future v2 must ship an explicit, reviewable migration workflow with check/dry-run
36	behavior before any command rewrites v1 data. Support for v1 will not be removed within package 0.x
37	or 1.x. Removing it later requires a package major release and a documented migration path.
38	
39	After the first beta tag, changes that make a previously accepted safe v1 configuration invalid are
40	breaking changes. A demonstrated security defect may require a narrower rejection, but it must be
41	documented in the changelog and covered by a regression test.
42	
43	## Rejected alternatives
44	
45	- **Treat the schema as the complete validator:** rejected because filesystem and normalized
46	  ownership rules cannot be represented accurately.
47	- **Silently normalize whitespace or paths:** rejected because the rendered value would differ from
48	  reviewed YAML.
49	- **Let the installed CLI reinterpret v1 over time:** rejected because repositories could change
50	  behavior without changing their canonical version.
51	- **Add a no-op migration command now:** rejected because it would create an interface without a
52	  real source/target transformation to validate.
53	
54	## Consequences
55	
56	- Schema/runtime parity needs a permanent generated and boundary corpus.
57	- New configuration concepts that cannot be added compatibly require v2.
58	- The copied schema is generated ownership and must participate in the same collision graph as every
59	  document and adapter.
60	- Older alpha repositories may receive a non-blocking editor-directive warning after upgrading.
61	
62	## Validation
63	
64	- Strict Ajv compilation and boundary tests for the public schema.
65	- A deterministic 500-case corpus proving runtime-accepted generated v1 configs pass the schema.
66	- Upgrade coverage for missing schema artifacts and missing YAML directives.
67	- Exact package and initialized-project schema byte comparisons.
68

1	# ADR-0009: Add explicit configuration v2 for universal agent surfaces
2	
3	- Status: Accepted
4	- Date: 2026-07-11
5	- Owners: Repository maintainer
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Configuration v1 is a published compatibility contract. It names Codex and Claude Code adapters
10	directly and has no continuity policy. Adding Cursor, Gemini CLI, generated Skills, or checkpoint
11	selection by silently changing v1 would make the same reviewed YAML mean something different after a
12	package upgrade.
13	
14	Codex and Cursor use the same repository instruction surface, while Claude Code and Gemini CLI use
15	distinct root files. Treating every harness as a separate adapter would duplicate `AGENTS.md`
16	ownership and create invalid output collisions.
17	
18	## Decision
19	
20	Carrylog supports configuration versions 1 and 2 concurrently. New `init` operations create v2;
21	existing v1 repositories remain valid and are never migrated by `sync`.
22	
23	Version 2 adds:
24	
25	- adapter surfaces `agents`, `claude`, and `gemini` rather than one entry per harness;
26	- `agents` as the shared `AGENTS.md` surface for Codex and Cursor;
27	- `continuity.checkpointDocument`, which must identify an always-loaded document;
28	- `continuity.generateSkills`, which controls deterministic repository Skill generation.
29	
30	Each version has a separate packaged JSON Schema and copied `.agent-context/config.schema.json`.
31	Runtime decoding rejects cross-version adapter names. Configuration v1 schema bytes, `$id`, marker
32	namespaces, and semantics remain frozen under ADR-0005 and ADR-0008.
33	
34	`carrylog migrate --to 2` is the only v1-to-v2 transition. It preserves YAML comments and LF/CRLF
35	style, maps `codex` to `agents`, and adds continuity policy. `--universal` ensures all three surfaces
36	and enables Skills; it can also complete a partial v2 configuration. A stock published v1 handoff is
37	converted automatically, and an already compliant checkpoint is preserved. Customized handoff prose
38	without the required checkpoint sections fails with `E_CHECKPOINT_REVIEW_REQUIRED` rather than being
39	semantically reclassified.
40	
41	Migration plans schema, adapter, Skill, checkpoint, and config changes before mutation. Unowned
42	adapter files still require `--adopt`; Skills are never adopted or merged. The config rename is last
43	in the guarded batch so a process failure cannot leave v2 claiming outputs that were not attempted.
44	This ordering narrows failure impact but does not claim an OS-level cross-file transaction.
45	
46	## Rejected alternatives
47	
48	- **Extend v1 in place:** rejected because it violates the published meaning of v1.
49	- **One adapter per harness:** rejected because Codex and Cursor would compete for `AGENTS.md`.
50	- **Implicit migration during `sync`:** rejected because customized handoff semantics require review.
51	- **Infer customized checkpoint sections with a model:** rejected because migration must remain
52	  deterministic, offline, and auditable.
53	- **Drop v1 after introducing v2:** rejected by the compatibility period in ADR-0005.
54	
55	## Consequences
56	
57	- Code paths and tests must keep version-specific adapter and schema contracts distinct.
58	- A user who wants all supported harnesses runs `migrate --to 2 --universal`; a narrower migration
59	  preserves the surfaces they selected.
60	- New harnesses should map to an existing discovery surface when ownership is truly shared, otherwise
61	  a future configuration version may be required.
62	- Generated Skill paths participate in normalized managed-path ownership only while Skills are
63	  enabled; disabling generation leaves existing managed Skills for explicit human removal and warns.
64	
65	## Validation
66	
67	- Strict schema/runtime tests for both versions and 500 generated valid v2 configurations.
68	- Partial v1 and v2 universal migrations, non-universal migration, idempotence, comment and CRLF
69	  preservation, output collisions, customized checkpoints, and unowned Skill conflicts.
70	- No-partial-write assertions for every planning conflict and config-last ordering review.
71	- Carrylog's own repository migration from v1 to universal v2 followed by clean sync and validation.
72

1	# Configuration reference
2	
3	`.agent-context/config.yaml` is canonical, reviewed project data. The copied
4	`.agent-context/config.schema.json` is generated editor support and is repaired by `carrylog sync`.
5	
6	## Version contract
7	
8	Configuration versions `1` and `2` are supported. Configuration version and npm package version are
9	separate; unknown versions and cross-version adapter names fail before any write.
10	
11	Version 1 is the frozen published compatibility contract. Version 2 adds universal agent surfaces and
12	continuity policy. New initialization creates v2, while existing v1 repositories remain valid and are
13	never rewritten implicitly. See [ADR-0005](decisions/0005-configuration-v1-compatibility.md) and
14	[ADR-0009](decisions/0009-configuration-v2-and-universal-surfaces.md).
15	
16	Every runtime-decoder-accepted configuration also passes its versioned public JSON Schema. JSON
17	Schema validation alone is insufficient: runtime checks additionally enforce normalized ownership,
18	checkpoint references, portable paths, symlink rejection, actual content budgets, and filesystem
19	state.
20	
21	The recommended first line enables YAML editor validation:
22	
23	```yaml
24	# yaml-language-server: $schema=./config.schema.json
25	```
26	
27	An older v1 file without this comment remains valid at runtime. `validate` emits
28	`W_CONFIG_SCHEMA_HEADER`; add the comment manually after review. `sync` does not rewrite canonical
29	YAML.
30	
31	## Fields
32	
33	### `version`
34	
35	Required integer. Must be `1` or `2`.
36	
37	### `project.name`
38	
39	Required single-line string, 1–120 Unicode characters. Leading/trailing whitespace and reserved
40	managed-marker text are rejected.
41	
42	### `documents`
43	
44	Required array with 1–256 entries and at least one `load: always` entry.
45	
46	| Field | Contract |
47	| --- | --- |
48	| `id` | Unique lowercase identifier matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, at most 64 characters |
49	| `path` | Unique path relative to `.agent-context/`, at most 1024 Unicode characters |
50	| `load` | `always` or `on-demand` |
51	| `description` | Single-line router description, at most 240 characters |
52	| `triggers` | Optional non-empty list of at most 32 single-line strings, each at most 120 characters |
53	
54	Document path uniqueness uses conservative Unicode compatibility and multi-step case normalization
55	for cross-platform safety. This can intentionally reject names that coexist on one filesystem when
56	another supported filesystem may alias them.
57	
58	Version 1 uses document ID `handoff` for `carrylog handoff`. Version 2 uses
59	`continuity.checkpointDocument`, whose target must exist and use `load: always`.
60	
61	The complete instructions template published in `@jaemani/agent-context-kit@0.1.0-beta.3` defines
62	the old-package-to-Carrylog migration boundary independently of a mutable document ID or path.
63	Carrylog can replace that exact template while
64	preserving LF or CRLF line endings. Customized always-loaded context with a command-shaped invocation
65	of the removed `ackit` executable is invalid until a maintainer reviews and changes the command;
66	historical prose and other human content are not inferred from a template.
67	
68	### `adapters`
69	
70	Required array with 1–32 entries.
71	
72	| Field | Contract |
73	| --- | --- |
74	| `type` | v1: `codex` or `claude`; v2: `agents`, `claude`, or `gemini` |
75	| `output` | Unique project-relative instruction-file path |
76	
77	The v2 `agents` surface is shared by Codex and Cursor and defaults to `AGENTS.md`; this avoids two
78	logical harnesses competing for one output. `claude` defaults to `CLAUDE.md`, and `gemini` defaults to
79	`GEMINI.md`.
80	
81	### `continuity` (v2 only)
82	
83	| Field | Contract |
84	| --- | --- |
85	| `checkpointDocument` | ID of one configured `load: always` document |
86	| `generateSkills` | Generate and validate the shared `.agents` Skill and Claude adapter Skill |
87	
88	When Skill generation is disabled, existing Carrylog-marked Skills are not deleted automatically;
89	`validate` warns so their removal remains an explicit reviewed action.
90	
91	The generated continuity Skill resolves executables offline in a fixed order: a compatible Carrylog
92	source build, the nearest compatible project-pinned package, then a compatible global installation.
93	Each selected candidate must support `resume`; an incompatible pinned candidate stops with explicit
94	guidance instead of falling through or downloading another version.
95	
96	Every config, document, copied schema, and adapter output has exclusive path ownership. Exact,
97	case-folded, or Unicode-normalized collisions fail before planning writes.
98	
99	### `policies`
100	
101	- `maxAlwaysCharacters`: total JavaScript character units allowed across `always` documents;
102	- `maxAdapterCharacters`: maximum generated managed block per adapter.
103	
104	Both are required integers from 1,000 through 100,000. These deterministic budgets are not claims
105	about a particular model tokenizer. Independently of those configurable rendering budgets, portable
106	resume observes at most 8 MiB across the configuration and all canonical documents in one pass. This
107	fixed aggregate read limit prevents a large on-demand catalog from multiplying per-file limits into
108	unbounded retained memory.
109	
110	## Portable path rules
111	
112	Paths use `/`, remain relative and normalized, and cannot contain `.`/`..` segments, empty segments,
113	NUL/control characters, Windows-reserved names/characters, trailing dots/spaces, or reserved marker
114	text. Existing symlink components are rejected. A valid-looking schema path can still fail runtime
115	ownership or filesystem checks.
116	
117	## Explicit v1 migration
118	
119	```bash
120	carrylog migrate --to 2 --universal --dry-run
121	carrylog migrate --to 2 --universal
122	carrylog validate
123	```
124	
125	Without `--universal`, migration preserves the selected v1 surfaces and leaves Skill generation
126	disabled. With it, Carrylog ensures `agents`, `claude`, and `gemini` surfaces and enables Skills. A
127	stock v1 handoff can be converted automatically; customized prose must already satisfy the checkpoint
128	section contract or migration stops with `E_CHECKPOINT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`.
129	
130	Migration preserves YAML comments and LF/CRLF style, preflights all outputs, and writes config last.
131	`--check` exits 1 when migration work remains; `--dry-run` prints the plan without writing.
132	
133	`sync`, `validate`, `handoff`, `checkpoint`, `migrate`, and `resume` discover the nearest
134	`.agent-context/config.yaml` while walking upward from the explicit or current root. They can
135	therefore run from a nested project directory. `init` treats its explicit or current root as the new
